The absence is real. WHY PARTIAL ANYWAY — A SEVERE DEFECT THAT NO NAMED CRITERION CATCHES: THE SURFACE REPORTS 'Unknown' FOR DATA IT ACTUALLY HOLDS. fixtures/plan-approval.v1.json session_scope contains sponsoring_human_id 'joe' and session_capability_profile 'read_and_propose-non-humanOnly'. The renderer at app.js line 219 asks for data.session_scope.sponsor and data.session_scope.capability. NEITHER KEY EXISTS in the fixture, so both resolve to undefined and print as Unknown. Three consequences, in ascending order of seriousness. First, the journey's own first task, determine exactly what an agent session is scoped and approved to do right now, cannot be completed from this surface, and 'inspect session scope' is a named step of this flow in the acceptance contract. Second, the SAME session SES-SYNTH-004 renders as scoped on the Work Request surface, capability read_and_propose from fixtures/work-request.v1.json line 34, and unscoped here, so two surfaces disagree about one session. Third and worst, this corrupts the meaning of Unknown across the entire product. Journey 7 PASSED precisely because Unknown is an honest signal that evidence is missing. Here Unknown means the renderer asked for a key that does not exist, and nothing on screen lets an operator tell an honest Unknown from a lookup failure. Every Unknown in the Control Room is now ambiguous evidence. THE SCORING LESSON, which belongs in Phase 0 exit rather than in this row alone: a criteria-only reading scores this journey green. The criteria are underspecified — they check that specific facts appear, and never that displayed values match the record behind them. This is the same shape as the 129-green-test finding: presence is asserted, truth is not. Control Room carries no route chips, so no coaching affordance applies. Timing not instrumented.

journeys.name: Release evidence and reconnect
journeys.task_statement: Check on a release in progress, confirm who is actually driving it, and verify it's proven safe with a working rollback.
pass_criteria: browser is not the operation owner
Complete requires version read-back and golden workflows
journeys.friction_notes: All three criteria met, one of them narrowly. (1) browser is not the operation owner — PASS, and shown two ways: an explicit 'Browser owns operation: false' field, and an authoritative event replay in which evt:004 deployment.reconnect_replayed reads 'browser resumed after evt:002', demonstrating the browser as a reconnecting observer rather than the owner of the operation. (2) sanctioned actuator is named — PASS, BUT ONLY ON THE AUDIT SCREEN AND ONLY AS AN EVIDENCE STRING. The audit chain carries 'evidence actuator:bin/deploy-worker.sh', and audit IS a declared screen for this flow, so the criterion is satisfied as written. It is nonetheless the weakest pass on the scorecard: fixtures/deployment.v1.json line 23 holds a full actuator object, name bin/deploy-worker.sh, registered true, invocation withheld, phase0_mode metadata_only, and the deployment renderer NEVER DISPLAYS IT. The only first-class actuator panel in the product is app.js line 182, which belongs to the SERVICE surface and is not a declared screen for this flow. None of this flow's three steps — open a synthetic rehearsal deployment, follow replayed server events, inspect verification and rollback readiness — route an operator to audit. So the fact is discoverable in principle and not on the path in practice. (3) Complete requires version read-back and golden workflows — PASS, and enforced rather than merely stated: the completion gate reads 'Complete only when target read-back and every named golden workflow pass', and the deployment is held at Partial with target version read-back Passed (expected 4435489, actual 4435489), worker health gate Passed, golden record workflow Pending, and a next action of 'Wait for the golden record workflow evidence'. The deployment does not present itself as complete while a named workflow is outstanding. THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SYSTEMIC CONTROL ROOM PATTERN, and the reason this row matters beyond its own result: THE FIXTURES HOLD FIELDS THE RENDERERS DROP. Journey 8 found configuration_fingerprint present per environment and absent from the environment table. Journey 10 found sponsoring_human_id and session_capability_profile present while the renderer asked for non-existent keys and printed Unknown. This journey finds actuator.name present in the deployment fixture and absent from the deployment surface. Three surfaces, three different fields, one failure mode: the record and the render have drifted apart, and the 129 green tests across both prototypes do not catch it because they assert that fields render, never that the record's contents reach the screen. This belongs in Phase 1 as a render-versus-record contract test, not as three separate bug fixes. SCORING DECISION RECORDED: whether criterion 2 counts was a judgment call, resolved by reading the contract rather than by asking Joe. flow-05's screens array is exactly ['deployment','audit'], which makes the audit naming in-scope and the criterion met. Had the array been deployment-only, this row would read fail. PRIOR EXPOSURE, disclosed: Joe had briefly landed on the deployment surface earlier in the session while journeys 7 and 8 were being scored, so this run was not fully cold. It does not change the result, because all three criteria were evaluated by direct inspection of the surface, the fixture and the contract rather than from his report. Control Room carries no route chips. Timing not instrumented.

journeys.name: Incident investigation to audit chain
journeys.task_statement: Investigate an active incident, separate what's confirmed from what's still a guess, and trace the full record of how it was handled.
journeys.friction_notes: All three criteria met, and this is the strongest surface pairing in either prototype. (1) restricted diagnostics are withheld — PASS: the audit surface carries an explicit redaction declaration, profile ops-safe-v1, withheld raw_output and authorization_material, with 'Secret values present: false' stated rather than implied; the incident surface exposes no raw diagnostic output anywhere. Withholding is declared, not merely absent. (2) resolution requires monitoring proof — PASS, and mechanically stated: a 'Resolution gate not met' callout reads '30 minutes monitoring and recovery evidence are required before Resolved', while the incident sits at state investigating with next action 'Verify whether the edge process or its heartbeat collector stopped'. The incident cannot present itself as resolved on assertion alone. (3) origin through verification is reconstructable — PASS, and completely: AUD-SYNTH-001 through AUD-SYNTH-007 form an unbroken causal chain from origin request.captured through agent_session, plan_revision, approval, execution and verification to release_or_incident, every entry carrying its resource, its cause pointing at the prior event id, its actor and its evidence ref, under an append-only policy showing update false, delete false, export false. THE BEST WORK ON EITHER PROTOTYPE, and it is what task clause 2 asked for: the incident surface separates Facts from Hypotheses STRUCTURALLY, not by tone. Two facts each carry a source and timestamp — 'The last accepted heartbeat was at 21:41Z' from managed-edge-heartbeat, 'The server record gateway remains reachable' from synthetic worker gate. Two hypotheses each carry an explicit Unconfirmed badge and the sentence 'Unconfirmed and displayed separately from facts'. An operator cannot mistake a guess for a finding, which is precisely the failure mode this journey exists to test. NOTABLE BEHAVIOUR UNDER A DEGRADED STATE, and a genuine positive: Joe selected the 'conflict' presentation state via the Control Room's scenario selector, one of ten authored states in fixtures/audit.v1.json. The surface then showed 'Conflict · The audit cursor expired. Reload from a current snapshot' with freshness dropping from fresh to unknown — AND THE FULL ORIGIN-TO-OUTCOME CHAIN STILL RENDERED BENEATH IT. Reconstructability survived the degraded state rather than being replaced by an error page, and the freshness field told the truth about itself while doing so. That is the correct behaviour and it contrasts sharply with journey 10, where Unknown was displayed for data the system actually held. PRIOR EXPOSURE, disclosed and not smoothed over: Joe passed through the audit surface earlier in the session while journey 7 was being scored, so this run was not fully cold. It does not change the result, because all three criteria were evaluated by direct inspection of both surfaces, the fixtures and the source rather than from his report. Control Room carries no route chips. Timing not instrumented.
